staudt.name: Karl Georg Christian von Staudt
staudt.role: German Geometer; Professor of Mathematics at Erlangen
staudt.bio: Founder of pure synthetic projective geometry (Geometrie der Lage, 1847) and the metric-free Algebra of Throws (Rechnung mit Würfen, Beiträge zur Geometrie der Lage, 1856–1860), liberating harmonic division, conics, and projective coordinates from metrical cross-ratios.

pasch.name: Moritz Pasch
pasch.bio: Author of Vorlesungen über neuere Geometrie (1882), which established the first rigorous axiomatization of linear betweenness and planar order (Pasch's Axiom), grounded projective ideal sheaves without appeal to infinity, and formulated the modern hypothetico-deductive method.

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.bio: Author of the Elements, whose implicit diagram-based assumptions on linear order and planar triangle separation (e.g., Elements I.16 and I.21) were explicitly exposed and axiomatized by Moritz Pasch in 1882.

pappus.name: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus.bio: Author of the Synagoge (Mathematical Collection), Book VII of which preserved the ancient theory of collinear cross-ratios, harmonic ranges, and the Hexagon Theorem (VII.139) later purified from metrical ratios by von Staudt.

desargues.name: Girard Desargues
desargues.role: French Architect, Engineer, and Projective Geometer
desargues.bio: Pioneer of perspective triangles, involutions, and points at infinity (Brouillon project, 1639), whose Two-Triangle Theorem underpins the uniqueness of von Staudt's quadrangle harmonic fourth and projective arithmetic.

pascal.name: Blaise Pascal
pascal.bio: Discoverer of the Hexagrammum Mysticum (1640) on inscribed hexagons in conics, derived purely synthetically in von Staudt's projective theory of polar systems and order curves.

brianchon.name: Charles Julien Brianchon
brianchon.bio: Formulator of Brianchon's Theorem (1806) on circumscribed hexagons of a conic, paired with Pascal's Theorem through projective reciprocity (polarity and duality) in von Staudt's Geometrie der Lage.

poncelet.name: Jean-Victor Poncelet
poncelet.bio: Author of the Traité des propriétés projectives des figures (1822), which revived synthetic projective geometry through central projection, continuity, and pole-polar duality.

mobius.name: August Ferdinand Möbius
mobius.bio: Author of Der barycentrische Calcul (1827), introducing barycentric coordinates, Möbius nets (rational harmonic scales generated by complete quadrangles), and projective collineations.

steiner.name: Jakob Steiner
steiner.bio: Author of Systematische Entwickelung (1832) and Die geometrischen Constructionen, ausgeführt mittelst der geraden Linie und Eines festen Kreises (1833), generating conics from projective pencils while still relying on metrical anharmonic ratios.

chasles.name: Michel Chasles
chasles.role: French Geometer and Historian of Geometry
chasles.bio: Systematizer of the metrical cross-ratio (rapport anharmonique) and homographies in Aperçu historique (1837) and Traité de géométrie supérieure (1852).

klein.name: Felix Klein
klein.role: German Mathematician; Author of the Erlangen Program
klein.bio: Unified Cayley's projective metrics with von Staudt's Geometrie der Lage (1871–1873), identifying the gap in von Staudt's continuity assumption for the Fundamental Theorem that led directly to Pasch's order axioms and Darboux's theorem.

darboux.name: Jean-Gaston Darboux
darboux.bio: Proved in 1880 that over the real field any mapping preserving harmonic tetrads is automatically continuous and induced by a genuine projective collineation, completing von Staudt's Fundamental Theorem over R.

hilbert.name: David Hilbert
hilbert.bio: Author of Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899), adopting Pasch's planar order axiom verbatim as Axiom II 4 and adapting von Staudt's algebra of throws into his Streckenrechnung (calculus of segments) in Chapter III.

russell.name: Bertrand Russell
russell.bio: Analyzed von Staudt's quadrangle construction and Pasch's order axiomatics in An Essay on the Foundations of Geometry (1897) and Part VI of The Principles of Mathematics (1903).

vailati.name: Giovanni Vailati
vailati.role: Italian Mathematician, Logician, and Historian of Science
vailati.bio: Collaborator of Giuseppe Peano who analyzed the logical properties of linear order and harmonic separation in the wake of Pasch's Vorlesungen (1895).

veblen.name: Oswald Veblen
veblen.bio: Co-author with J. W. Young of Projective Geometry (1910–1918), synthesizing von Staudt's algebra of throws and Pasch-Hilbert order axioms over arbitrary division rings and fields.

hoenen.name: Peter Hubert Jacob Hoenen, S.J.
hoenen.role: Dutch Philosopher of Mathematics; Professor at the Gregorian University
hoenen.bio: Author of De Noetica Geometriae (1954), contrasting Pasch's empiricist genesis and formalist deduction with Aristotelian-Thomistic noetic abstraction from intelligible matter.

tarski.name: Alfred Tarski
tarski.bio: Formulated first-order elementary geometry using only points, equidistance, and betweenness, adopting a five-point inner/outer form of Pasch's Axiom as his sole planar order postulate.
